states.name: Central Greece
timeline: Boeotia under Thebes, Phocis with the oracle of Delphi, and Euboea
Delium: a later legend has Socrates rescue Xenophon here, when he was a small child
At Socrates' suggestion, Xenophon consults Apollo at Delphi before leaving for Asia
Coronea: Xenophon fights beside King Agesilaus of Sparta against Thebes and Athens
Xenophon dedicates an offering at Delphi, then leaves the battlefield behind
Leuctra: Thebes breaks Sparta's power on land

states.name: Attica
timeline: Xenophon, son of Gryllus, is born in the deme of Erchia, east of Athens, around 430
Athens surrenders to Sparta; the Thirty rule the city, led by Socrates' former companion Critias
Democracy and an amnesty are restored
Xenophon leaves for Asia to join Cyrus; he will never live in Athens again
Athens tries and executes Socrates; Xenophon is far away in Asia
Exiled by decree, at the latest after fighting against Athens at Coronea (the date is disputed)
Athens allies with Sparta; his exile is probably lifted, and his sons serve in the Athenian cavalry
Xenophon's last work, Ways and Means, offers Athens advice on its revenues

states.name: Peloponnese
timeline: Sparta and its Peloponnesian League, Athens' enemy in the war Xenophon grows up in
Xenophon serves Sparta's King Agesilaus; Sparta becomes his patron
After Leuctra, Xenophon and his family move to Corinth
Mantinea: his son Gryllus dies fighting in the Athenian cavalry
Xenophon dies, probably soon after 355, by one ancient report at Corinth

states.name: West Greece
timeline: Elis, which hosts the Olympic Games, with Achaea and Aetolia
Sparta defeats Elis (c. 402–398) and strips it of its southern districts, where Scillus lies
Scillus, near Olympia: the Spartans settle the exile there (c. 394–390); he builds a shrine to Artemis
The Eleans retake Scillus; Xenophon leaves, and is later pardoned by the Olympic Council

events.title: Born at Erchia
events.text: Xenophon, son of Gryllus, is born to a wealthy family of the deme of Erchia, around 430 (the year is an estimate).

events.title: Plague in Athens
events.text: Plague sweeps the crowded city in the second year of the war with Sparta.

events.title: Delium legend
events.text: Diogenes Laertius and Strabo say Socrates saved Xenophon in this battle. Xenophon was about six: the story cannot be true.

events.title: The Clouds
events.text: Aristophanes mocks Socrates on stage as a crank who studies the sky and teaches cheating.

events.title: Callias' party
events.text: Xenophon's Symposium is set at a banquet of 422 or 421 and claims he was there, as a boy of about eight.

events.title: Alcibiades sails
events.text: Socrates' most famous companion leads the fleet to Sicily, then defects to Sparta.

events.title: Socrates says no
events.text: Presiding in the Assembly, Socrates refuses an illegal vote against the generals; Xenophon records it twice.

events.title: Aegospotami
events.text: Sparta captures Athens' last fleet in the Hellespont; the city is starved into surrender.

events.title: The Thirty
events.text: Critias, once Socrates' companion, leads the Thirty, who ban the teaching of 'the art of words'.

events.title: Munichia
events.text: The democrats defeat the Thirty above Piraeus; Critias is killed and an amnesty follows.

events.title: Ask the god
events.text: Xenophon asks Apollo which gods to pray to for a safe journey; Socrates scolds him for the question.

events.title: Sardis
events.text: Xenophon joins Cyrus' army, invited by his friend Proxenus. Cyrus marches inland against his brother, the Persian king.

events.title: Byzantium
events.text: After Cyrus' death in Babylonia, Xenophon has led the survivors back to the sea; he stops them from sacking the city.

events.title: Sparta beats Elis
events.text: Sparta's war on Elis (c. 402–398) ends with Elis giving up its southern districts, where Scillus lies.

events.title: Socrates executed
events.text: Athens condemns Socrates for impiety and corrupting the young; he drinks the poison in prison.

events.title: Pergamum
events.text: Xenophon hands the survivors over to the Spartan general Thibron for war on the Persian governors.

events.title: Agesilaus at Ephesus
events.text: Sparta's king makes Ephesus his base for war on Persia; Xenophon serves with him.

events.title: Aulis
events.text: Agesilaus sacrifices before sailing for Asia; Boeotian horsemen break up the rite.

events.title: Battle near Sardis
events.text: Agesilaus defeats the Persian cavalry by the Pactolus river; Xenophon is with him in Asia.

events.title: Amphipolis
events.text: Marching home through Thrace, Agesilaus hears of Sparta's victory at Nemea.

events.title: Narthacium
events.text: Agesilaus' cavalry defeats the Thessalian horsemen, in Xenophon's telling the king's proudest fight.

events.title: Coronea
events.text: Xenophon fights for Sparta against a coalition that includes Athens. Exile from Athens follows, if it had not already.

events.title: The tithe
events.text: Xenophon leaves Artemis' share of his spoils with the temple warden at Ephesus.

events.title: An offering at Delphi
events.text: Apollo's share goes into the Athenians' treasury at Delphi, inscribed with his name and Proxenus'.

events.title: The accuser's pamphlet
events.text: Around now the orator Polycrates publishes an 'Accusation of Socrates'; Xenophon's Memorabilia seems to answer it.

events.title: Scillus
events.text: The Spartans settle the exile near Olympia (c. 394–390); the Ephesian warden, visiting the Games, returns the tithe.

events.title: Artemis' shrine
events.text: With the tithe he builds a small copy of the temple of Ephesus, and holds a yearly feast and hunt.

events.title: Plato's Academy
events.text: Plato, Socrates' other great witness, begins teaching in a grove outside Athens.

events.title: Writing Socrates
events.text: At Scillus and later Corinth, Xenophon writes his Socratic works; their dates are unknown.

events.title: Leuctra
events.text: Thebes defeats Sparta; Spartan power in the Peloponnese collapses.

events.title: Scillus lost
events.text: The Eleans retake Scillus; Xenophon and his family leave for Corinth.

events.title: Pardoned
events.text: By Pausanias' account, the Olympic Council tries Xenophon for accepting land from Sparta, and pardons him.

events.title: Corinth
events.text: Xenophon settles at Corinth, where he will spend his last years.

events.title: Athens and Sparta allied
events.text: Old enemies join against Thebes; Xenophon's exile is probably lifted around now.

events.title: Aristotle arrives
events.text: The seventeen-year-old Aristotle joins Plato's Academy; he will later call Socratic dialogues a literary genre.

events.title: Mantinea
events.text: Gryllus, Xenophon's son, dies in the Athenian cavalry. An Athenian tradition said he struck down the Theban general Epaminondas.

events.title: The history ends
events.text: Xenophon closes his Greek history with Mantinea: let another write what came after.

events.title: Ways and Means
events.text: His last work proposes ways to raise Athens' revenues, from silver mines to resident foreigners.

events.title: Death
events.text: Xenophon dies some time after 355, in his mid-seventies; one ancient report places his death at Corinth.

eras: Asia, and the death of Socrates
chartNote: Share of the area of modern Greece, by Xenophon's tie to each present-day region in a given year. Regions are today's boundaries and stand for the one place in them that mattered to him (Scillus for West Greece, Sparta and later Corinth for the Peloponnese). The dates of his exile, of his estate at Scillus and of the end of his exile are disputed or approximate; Asia, where he spent 401–394, lies off the regions. A simplification.
